Q: Roblox Lua: House generator stops running when math.random picks a duplicate number A:

Generating a random number in a loop in the hope of getting a new value within a narrow range is bad practice (although it doesn’t affect the uniformity of the distribution, the time complexity will no longer be a pure O(1)). It’s better to immediately exclude the old value from the range:

local HouseModels = {'M1', 'M2', 'M3', 'M4', 'M5'}
local OldNum = math.random(#HouseModels) -- for 1st uniform distribution

for i = 1, 10 do
    local r = math.random(#HouseModels - 1)
    local RandomIndex = (OldNum + r - 1) % #HouseModels + 1
    print(string.format(
        '(%d + %d - 1) %% %d + 1 = %d',
        OldNum, r, #HouseModels, RandomIndex))
    OldNum = RandomIndex  
end

Possible result:

(4 + 3 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 2
(2 + 3 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 5
(5 + 1 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 1
(1 + 2 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 3
(3 + 3 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 1
(1 + 3 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 4
(4 + 3 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 2
(2 + 4 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 1
(1 + 4 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 5
(5 + 1 - 1) % 5 + 1 = 1

Q: Cookies from server aren't coming with the request A:

The 500 error on chunk 2 usually points to a broken sticky session or session affinity loss because the pod handling the upload can't identify the initial state without that cookie.

If Chrome isn't storing or receiving the Set-Cookie header on the first request, a few common things could be happening here.

First off, check the devtools Network tab for the first chunk response specifically under the Headers tab. Look at the Set-Cookie header if present. Chrome will often show a small warning icon next to dropped cookies indicating why it rejected them (e.g., SameSite attribute missing or mismatched Secure flags on non-HTTPS origins).

Another thing is your --incognito flag alongside your prefs. Modern Chrome builds tend to override custom flags regarding third-party cookies and cross-site context inside incognito mode regardless of profile.block_third_party_cookies settings. Try dropping --incognito temporarily to rule out browser security policy enforcement.

If the upload request is being triggered via XHR/Fetch on the UI layer, make sure the frontend client actually includes credentials (withCredentials: true for Axios/XHR or credentials: 'include' for fetch). Otherwise, Chrome strips incoming Set-Cookie headers from the store even if the server sent them.

To narrow this down, I'd suggest testing the first chunk endpoint outside Selenium using Postman or curl -v to capture the raw response headers:

curl -v -X POST "YOUR_ENDPOINT" -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" ...

If curl receives the Set-Cookie header but Selenium doesn't, it's definitely a Chrome/driver policy issue. If curl doesn't receive it either, the issue is on the backend/ingress side (e.g., standard ingress controllers not appending session cookies before hitting a 500 downstream).

Could you share the raw response headers of the first chunk request if possible? That would help isolate whether it's a driver/browser rejection or a backend response failure.

Q: Setting up friendly URLs using urlrewriter.net shows actual URL A:

To mask the URL and keep the friendly address in the browser, try to add the processing="rewriting" attribute to your <redirect> tag. Alternatively, depending on the version of the URLRewriter.net library used, you should use the <rewrite> tag instead of <redirect>

Try 1: Use rewrite tag:
<rewrite url="~/products/(.+)/(.+)" to="~/Default.aspx?category=$1&type=$2" />

Try 2: : Explicitly set processing attribute:
<redirect url="~/products/(.+)/(.+)" to="~/Default.aspx?category=$1&type=$2" processing="rewriting" />

Q: How to summarise hourly data of the Formal class 'Period'? A:

In base:

df |>
  subset(outcome == 1) |>
  with(data = _, table(hour = time@hour)) |>
  as.data.frame(responseName = "n")

#>    hour  n
#> 1     0 52
#> 2     1 52
#> 3     2 44
#> 4     3 52
#> 5     4 50
#> ...
